correctness.rationale: Every closure extent is classified by empty, singleton, unique-common-vertex and empty-intersection cases. The minimum-degree and simplicity hypotheses ensure all concept types are distinct. Stability counts follow from disjoint subset classes and the handshaking identity; the graph is recovered as the nonbottom-meet graph of coatoms; and triangle counts distinguish arbitrarily many regular-graph witnesses. Reproducible direct enumeration checked 266 graphs and 37,624 edge-subsets, including the cubic pair. Boundary cases are handled by explicit assumptions and the proof, not extrapolation from computation.

value.rationale: An exact formula for a standard FCA robustness metric reveals a substantive representational limitation: the entire unlabelled distribution discards all graph adjacency beyond degrees, while its source lattice remains fully faithful. It is not a rephrasing of the definition of stability, as the theorem gives a uniform graph-class classification, proves order reconstruction and exhibits t+1 distinct isomorphism types with identical full spectra for every t. This bears directly on attempts to compare contexts using stability summaries and separates a canonical lattice invariant from its lossy numerical projection.
